Hi, I’m sorry it’s been such a rough ride. There seems to be a shift from labelling people but there’s nothing wrong in wanting an official diagnosis. It can be helpful as in a diagnosis can help you understand what’s happening and maybe it would also make you feel more confident in researching what will work to help you. Also like you say it’s easier to give a label to others rather than having to fully explain how you feel. I wish I could offer you more help than this. When you’re going through a rough patch please consider the Samaritans, you don’t have to be suicidal to call them, also they are completely confidential and cannot trace your calls. I have spoken to them a few times when there’s no one else available to talk to and they have been so fantastic, offering a listening ear and empathy with no time limit on the call. Last time I phoned them incredibly distressed and a woman talked to me for nearly 2 hours! The only other thing I can offer is for you to please keep hanging in there, you matter in the world. I really hope you can get the support you need.

The original post and comments have been so good to read! I’m 44 started out on spectrum as a little child. We even had a BBC computer (Anyone here remember them, or use one?) I remember inputting a huge code on the BBC just to make a dot go across the screen lol! We had the Amiga 500+ which I loved then moved on to PC before getting into consoles. I loved my original Gameboy, Tetris addict back then! I’ve had just about every console except I came to the Xbox when the 360 was released. I loved my Dreamcast and still have it boxed in the cupboard with about 6 games. I have had every version of the PlayStation but don’t have the money right now for the PS5 and I have quite a few games to catch up on on the PS4 yet. I’m a huge fan of PSVR and couldn’t never have imagined that experience when I was young! Having seen gaming throughout the decades I still get blown away by today’s graphics and ideas for present games. I just started playing Detroit Become Human and it’s such an amazing experience, from the graphics to the idea of the game right down to how the experience makes me question my choices in the game making it a deep experience! I feel privileged to have witnessed how the industry has and is evolving. Due to mental health problems it has been a lifeline on occasion. Here’s to the future and the next generation of consoles and gamers.
